sections.label: HDB polling and vesting provisions
sections.summary: Extends polling provisions to ROS upgrading works and removes the requirement to state lodgement or recission dates in HDB notices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: First, it will extend existing polling provisions for HDB's upgrading programmes to also cover upgrading works at HDB commercial sites carried out under the Revitalisation of Shops Scheme, or in short, the ROS Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Second, it removes the requirement for the date of lodgement or date of recission to be stated in HDB's notice served under Section 59(2) to 59(4).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In place of this, provisions have been introduced to prevent the Board from lodging the instrument of vesting or rescinding the agreement for a lease until after the expiry of the period during which the purchaser, personal representatives or any interested persons may appeal to the Minister.

sections.label: MND reviews ROS scheme
sections.summary: MND proposes adjusting the ROS scheme to allow upgrading if 75% of shop owners vote in favour.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Instead, a refresh of the physical environment will be a win-win – residents can enjoy a better shopping experience, and shop operators may gain more customers over time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Therefore, MND has reviewed the ROS and is proposing to adjust the scheme to allow upgrading to proceed if 75% of the shop owners vote in favour of the upgrading.

sections.label: Clause 5 amends section 77
sections.summary: Clause 5 lets HDB poll shop owners and proceed with upgrading works when at least 75% of votes are in favour.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 5 amends section 77 to allow HDB to conduct a poll of the HDB shop owners for the purpose of shop upgrading works within an HDB commercial precinct and allows for the works to proceed when at least 75% of the votes by shop owners are in favour of the upgrading works.

sections.label: Studying co-payment structure enhancements
sections.summary: Further enhancements to the co-payment structure are being studied, including lowering shop owners' co-payment share.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To support our heartland businesses in their rejuvenation efforts, we are studying further enhancements to the co-payment structure, including lowering the co-payment share of shop owners.

sections.label: Heartland Shops Study results
sections.summary: HDB's November 2022 Heartland Shops Study found seven in 10 residents visit heartland shops at least weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In November 2022, HDB released the result of the Heartland Shops Study which reveal that seven out of 10 residents surveyed visit the heartland shops at least once a week and about one-third of their monthly expenditure is spent at heartland shops.

sections.label: Number of HDB shops
sections.summary: HDB states there are about 15,000 shops across town centres, neighbourhood areas and precinct shop clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: According to HDB, there are a total of about 15,000 shops spread out across town centres, neighbourhood areas and precinct shop clusters that are either rented out by HDB or owned by private operators.

sections.label: Marine Parade merchants ROS funding
sections.summary: Marine Parade Merchants' Association failed to secure ROS funding, so the speaker supports letting HDB poll and proceed with 75% shop owner approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, Marine Parade Merchants' Association tried to secure the ROS funding on several occasions but did not succeed on any one of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support the proposed amendment to the Act to allow HDB to carry out polling for the upgrading works or ROS and to allow the works to proceed when at least 75% of the shop owners vote in favour of the works.

sections.label: Voting rights by shop size
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether HDB will distinguish commercial properties by size, giving a supermarket-sized shop the same voting right as a small shop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, for the poll of the prescribed owners of commercial property, will HDB distinguish between commercial properties of different sizes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Will a big shop, say for example the size of a supermarket, be given the same voting right as a small shop regardless of the size of the shop unit?

sections.label: Balancing upgrading and maintenance costs
sections.summary: The speaker asks how HDB balances the need to upgrade common areas against possibly higher long-run maintenance costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: How does HDB balance the need to upgrade the common area versus the possible higher maintenance costs in the long run?

sections.label: Online share of retail sales
sections.summary: SingStat data shows online sales were about 12% to 15% of total retail sales in 2022, up from mid-single digits in 2018 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on SingStat data, online sales now represent about 12% to 15% of total retail sales in 2022, up from the mid-single digit percentages during the pre-pandemic periods from 2018 to 2019.

sections.label: Reducing shop owner approval threshold
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes clause 5 reducing the threshold for shop owners to approve upgrading works from 100% to 75% of total value in votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moving on to the specifics of the Bill, I welcome the move to reduce the threshold for shop owners to approve upgrading works from 100% to 75% of the total value in votes under clause 5.

sections.label: HDB shop tender criteria weightage
sections.summary: Changes to Price Quality Method tenders for HDB shops from first half 2023 raise business concept and affordability weightage from 25% to 30%-35% to 45%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is the proactive curation of the tenant mix or trade mix.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note changes to the Price Quality Method tenders for HDB shops which will apply to new tenders starting in the first half of 2023, where the weightage for the business concept and affordability criteria will be raised from the current 25% to 30% to 35% to 45%.

sections.label: Heartland merchants going digital
sections.summary: 93% of heartland merchants now accept e-payments, with residents conditioned to scanning QR codes due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With residents conditioned to the scanning of QR codes because of COVID-19, it is heartening to hear that today 93% of heartland merchants have gone digital in the form of accepting e-payments.

sections.label: Rivervale division retail offerings
sections.summary: Rivervale Plaza and Rivervale Mall offer retail, but the division has only one coffee shop and one convenience store.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Within my Rivervale division for example, while it is great that Rivervale Plaza and Rivervale Mall provide various retail offerings for those living in the immediate vicinity, there is only one coffee shop and one convenience store in the entire division.

sections.label: Reviving convenience and coffee shops
sections.summary: The Workers' Party calls for HDB to allocate void deck space or repurpose underutilised multi-storey car parks for coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party has called for a revival of convenience and coffee shops where HDB should allocate a portion of void deck space to provide for at least one coffee shop for every two precincts, or perhaps we could also consider repurposing certain parts of our multi-storey car parks (MSCPs) which are underutilised to allow commercial spaces even if not for coffee shops.

sections.label: Expiring shop leases treatment
sections.summary: HDB explained that shops with expiring 30-year leases will return to HDB and be let out via a tenancy model.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: HDB has explained that the treatment of shops' expiring 30-year leases will be returned to HDB to be let out to operators via a tenancy model.

sections.label: Commercial property upgrading owner consensus
sections.summary: Clause 5 amendment 2 requires 75% owner consensus for commercial property upgrading works, and clarification is sought on effecting this.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In clause 5 amendment 2 section 77, where a precinct has been declared to carry out the polling connection, with a proposal for the commercial property upgrading works, an approval seeks for at least 75% of the owner consensus before these works can be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While I understand this concept of approval is similar to other schemes, like the Home Improvement Project, the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme, but the probability of flats changing owners are generally higher and new flat owners would mostly renovate post-purchase to upkeep their units.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to seek clarification from the Senior Minister if State how this amendment can be effected if the sold commercial shops already constitute more than 25% and the likelihood of getting owners onboard to rejuvenate their shops and the neighbourhood is low.

sections.label: Commercial upgrading works approval vote
sections.summary: The Bill requires commercial property upgrading works to be approved by a 75% vote of benefiting owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, it may not always be clear that such works, when proposed, achieve such a goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: That is why for commercial property upgrading works, the Bill requires the works to be approved by a 75% vote of the owners who will benefit from the works.

sections.label: HDB cost recovery provision
sections.summary: New section 78(3A) lets HDB recover commercial property upgrading costs from every owner and the responsible Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 78(3A) will allow HDB to recover the costs of commercial property upgrading works from every owner of such property and the Town Council responsible for the maintenance of common property.

sections.label: Excess upgrading cost question
sections.summary: A Member asks who bears excess costs when upgrading costs exceed initial estimates, since recovery occurs only after works are completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that the recovery of costs is to be done only after HDB has completed the upgrading works, where the cost exceeds initial estimates, can the Senior Minister of State confirm who will bear the excess costs?

sections.label: Excluding no-response votes
sections.summary: A Member suggests MND consider having HDB exclude no-response votes if over 70% of shop owners have responded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The second point I would MND to consider is, can HDB consider excluding the no-response from the vote, if more than 70% of the shop owners have responded?

sections.label: Low-cost preliminary design concept
sections.summary: A Member suggests HDB work with MAs on a low-cost preliminary design concept detailing likely works so shop owners know what they pay for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The third suggestion I have is, it would be wonderful if HDB can work with MAs to come up with a low-cost preliminary design concept and detail out the works that would likely be done, so that the shop owners will know what they are paying for.

sections.label: Prioritising add-on ROS projects
sections.summary: A Member suggests HDB prioritise ROS projects that can be added to existing upgrading efforts such as ROHS or Town Council renovations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Beyond these three suggestions on generating consensus, I would also like to suggest that HDB consider prioritising ROS projects that can be added on to existing upgrading efforts – be it ROHS efforts to revitalise a town or when there is a plan by the local Town Council to do extensive renovations at the town centres.

sections.label: Parity for all shop owners
sections.summary: If a poll succeeds, HDB will recover upgrading costs from all beneficiary shop owners regardless of their vote or attendance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Next, if a poll succeeds, I believe Members would agree, that there is a need for parity for all shop owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Hence, HDB will recover the cost of upgrading from all beneficiary shop owners, regardless of their vote or their attendance at the poll.

sections.label: Upgrading support threshold balance
sections.summary: A 75% threshold, drawn from the Home Improvement Programme, is used to balance support for upgrading with shop owners who may not support it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: At the same time, we have to strike a reasonable balance with the consideration that some individual shop owners might not support upgrading for their own reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have hence taken a leaf from other upgrading programmes, such as the Home Improvement Programme (HIP), where the threshold of 75% has come to be widely accepted.

sections.label: Voting rights per beneficiary unit
sections.summary: Shop owners get one vote per beneficiary unit regardless of the size of the commercial property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: On Mr Lim's query on whether voting rights will differ based on the size of the commercial property, shop owners will be entitled one vote per beneficiary unit, regardless of size.

sections.label: ROS upgrading works menu
sections.summary: The ROS scheme offers jointly funded upgrading works, with main items and shop-specific items that individual shops can opt in for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Currently, there is a menu of upgrading works offered under the ROS scheme, which are funded jointly by shop owners, HDB and the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Main items include fixed awnings, re-tiling, shop corridor lightings, digital directory, way-finders, landscaping and street furniture and Digital Display Panels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Shop-specific items that individual shops can opt in for include vertical blinds and roller shutters.

sections.label: F&B planning parameters
sections.summary: HDB follows planning parameters for inserting food and beverage and other amenities needed by residents when planning and building each town.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As for the specifics, with regards to the injection of eating places in our towns, HDB follows planning parameters for the insertion of food and beverage (F&B), as well as other kinds of amenities and facilities needed by residents as we plan and build each town.

sections.label: Enhancing ROS scheme polling
sections.summary: The ROS scheme is enhanced with formal polling provisions to support heartland merchants and facilitate physical upgrading, and the citation year changes to 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We know that our heartland shops hold a very special place in the hearts of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Hence, we are giving more support our heartland merchants through enhancing the ROS scheme with formal polling provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Overall, the amendments will enable us to better facilitate physical upgrading, which is a first and necessary step in our plans to refresh and upkeep the vibrancy of our heartland shop precincts.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2022" will be changed to "2023", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
